title: Len Johnson: Site revealed for Manchester boxing statue

input.lead: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
input.summary: Manchester could get its first Black city-centre statue after years of campaigning
input.evidence_text: He was one of Britain's best boxers, but never became champion Born in Clayton, Manchester, in 1902, Len Johnson won more than 90 fights during his career but was barred from contesting the British title because of the colour of his skin He later channelled the fighting spirit he showed in the ring into campaigning against racism, becoming a trade unionist, civil rights activist and member of the Communist Party More than 50 years after his death, Johnson is set to become the first black person to be honoured with a statue in Manchester. But who was Len Johnson? Despite having little boxing knowledge or training, he got his first taste of the sport after a fight at work prompted his father, a former boxer, to take him to a local contest A few weeks later, after training by skipping with an old washing line, he stepped into the ring for his first bout at the Alhambra Theatre in Openshaw

input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester has diagnosed the most lung cancers in the country as part of Lung Cancer Screening, as the NHS encourages more people to take up their lung health check when they get their invite The city is one of the first areas in England to roll out NHS lung cancer screening across all 10 of its localities, achieving the national target four years ahead of schedule New figures released at the start of Lung Cancer Awareness Month in November reveal that 1,829 lung cancers have now been diagnosed through the NHS Lung Cancer Screening Programme in Greater Manchester, with more than 80% detected at an earlier stage, giving people more treatment The targeted programme invites people registered with a GP in Greater Manchester who are aged 55 to 74 and who currently smoke or have smoked in the past for a lung health check on a mobile clinic which tours the city. title: More than £3m of support secured for Mancunians through game-changing Citizens Advice hospital trial

input.lead: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
input.summary: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges
input.evidence_text: Manchester hospitals have become a focal point not only for improving people’s health but supporting them overcome financial or housing challenges In December 2023 a trial was launched to embed two Citizens Advice case workers in two Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) run hospitals in Manchester - the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and North Manchester General Hospital This was further expanded in June 2024 to include Wythenshawe Hospital, and the MRI in March 2025, and St Mary's in December 2025 with funding through MFT’s charity, as well as a damp and mould focused case worker funded through Manchester City Council The team of six Citizens Advice caseworkers are aimed at providing better wrap around care for patients and addressing the link we know exists between poor health, economic hardship and housing issues The trial has been a huge success with more than 1,500 people supported across the trial locations With more up to 3m patients contacts across MFT each year this presented a huge opportunity to reach people who may otherwise have not known about the services provided by Citizens Advice, or the support they were eligible to claim

input.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

title: Bolton Car Boot Sale

input.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
input.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
